newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt mostly lower in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt mostly lower in late trade.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mixed in late afternoon trade, but market participants said fixed-rate Brady instruments were mostly lower amid growing uncertainty about the U.S. interest rate environment.

"I think everyone realizes that Latin America is doing reasonably well but I think the big question mark that remains is the interest rate environment," said Kurt Schmid, executive director at SBC Warburg in New York. "I think there is indeed a huge uncertainty."
At 1700 EST, Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were down 3/8 at 62-1/8 and Mexico pars MX625L19=RR were off 1/8 at 72-3/4.

Although the fundamentals in Latin America continue to be acceptable and to gradually improve, Schmid said he believes the Brady sector will be much more vulnerable to any significant change in the U.S. interest rate enviroment.
Sources said the drop in the U.S. Treasury market also pressured some Brady bonds.
Nonetheless, market sources said new issuers should tap the markets now while the interest rate environment remains favorable.
"I do believe that for new issuers it would be a good time to approach the market as soon as possible," one said.
Indeed, Mexico is set to offer a $1.0 billion 10-year global bond via Merrill Lynch and Salomon Brothers.
In addition, sources said Argentina is expected to issue a $2.0 billion two-part global debt offering consisting of five and 20-year debt next week.
One source noted that a $2.0 billion offering by Argentina would take some pressure off since they have a big refunding requirement in 1997.

Meanwhile, Bulgarian Bradies suffered big losses amid confusion following the resignation of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov but sources said they still expect the country to meet its debt payments later this month.

"I do believe that it (the debt payment) will be made irrespective of the fact of whether they have agreed on a currency board but clearly the political vacuum doesn't help because Bulgaria will need decisive leadership to make the changes happen," said one market source.
"I personally would assume that the Brady payment at the end of January is not in jeopardy," the source added.
Nonetheless, Bulgaria's IABs BGFLTH=RR were off 7/8 at 49-7/8 and its FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were down 1/2 at 36-7/8.
Elsewhere in the Brady market, Brazil discount Z bonds BRFLTD24=RR were 1/8 firmer at 77-7/8 and Venezuelan par bonds VZ675C20=RR were 3/8 lower at 75-1/8.
